correctness.rationale: For every odd prime power, the conic has q+1 projective isotropic directions and q² points. Their exact hyperplane incidences give cone character sums q eta(-Q(z)); on the cone the quadratic-character difference kernel reduces to (q-1)(J-I) on q+1 character-weighted line vectors. Hence cone Gram eigenvalues are q³ (1), q² (q²-q-1), and q (q). Complementary principal blocks of a unitary q³-point Fourier matrix share all singular values except q³ repeated by the size difference q³-2q². This proves the final multiset, full invertibility, and condition q. Standalone q=3,5,7,9 checks passed, including nonprime q=9, but are only finite corroboration.

value.rationale: Nonsingular binary symmetric forms form a natural entire rank stratum. The theorem is a complete exact Fourier recovery/stability classification for every odd prime power, not a finite numerical observation: it gives all three spectral levels and multiplicities and sharp condition number q. Existing quadratic-cone extension bounds and ambient symmetric-form translation spectra do not directly provide the square principal Fourier sampling condition, so the exact stability law fills a motivated mathematical gap.
